chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The polytheists used to depart (from Arafat) before the sun set, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) opposed them, and he departed after the setting of the sun.'

He said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When the sun sets, depart with the people, and upon you should be tranquility and dignity, and depart with seeking forgiveness, for indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: Then hasten on from where the people hasten on and seek the forgiveness of Allah; surely Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.'

So when you reach the red dune on the right of the road, say: 'O Allah, have mercy on my standing, increase my knowledge, safeguard my religion for me, and accept my rituals.' Beware of the excitement which the people do, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O people, Hajj is not the excitement of cavalry, nor the racing of camels, but fear Allah and walk with a beautiful walk, do not trample the weak, nor trample a Muslim, be considerate and moderate in walking, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would restrain his she-camel until its head would touch the front of the saddle, and he would say: O people, upon you is calmness, thus the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is to be followed.'

Muawiya said, 'And I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: O Allah, emancipate me from the Fire,' and he repeated it until he departed. So I said to him, 'Are you not departing, for the people have already departed?' So he said, 'I fear the congestion, and I fear that I might participate in impeding a person.'

key_terms.الْكَثِيبِ الْأَحْمَرِ: The red dune (a landmark near Arafat)

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended etiquettes and actions for departing from Arafat during Hajj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the Sunnah of the Farewell Stand (Wudu') from Arafat, contrasting the Prophet's deliberate, dignified departure with the pre-Islamic practice of hasty rushing. It highlights the spiritual significance of seeking forgiveness (Istighfar) during the journey and emphasizes physical moderation (Daw') to prevent injury to the weak, reflecting the Shia emphasis on emulating the Prophet's gentle conduct. The narration also underscores the importance of avoiding the 'Wajif' (rushing) that leads to congestion and potential harm among pilgrims.
